The graph $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Then,

${\int }_{-5}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the line segment for $x\in [-5,0],$ the line segment for $x\in (0,3],$ and the line segment for $x\in [3,5].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-5}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{3}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-5,0].$   The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+4)(5) \\  & =\frac{25}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (0,3].$    The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3+0)(3) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,5].$   The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(0+2)(2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{3}=-2.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}-{A}_{3} \\  & =\frac{25}{2}+\frac{9}{2}-2 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$
